 Mr. M.M.Agnihotri, counsel for Appellant.
 Mr. C.A.Babrekar, counsel for Respondent No.1.
 Mr. Ujjawal Phasate, A.G.P. for Respondent No. 2

---------------------------------------------------------------------
 CORAM: NEERAJ P. DHOTE, J.
 DATE : 06/01/2026  JUDGMENT :
-
1) This appeal is filed by the acquiring body against the judgment and award dated 19/06/2013,
passed by the learned Civil Judge (Senior Division), Achalpur, District Kavita.
2/4 14 fa 14-15 Amravati (hereinafter referred to as 'Reference Court'), awarding the rate of Rs.50,000/- per hectare to the respondent/claimant for acquisition of his land admeasuring 2H 23R for MIDC purpose.
Maharashtra Industrial Development ... vs Suresh Uttamrao Kadu And Another on 6 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60494716/
1 2)
Heard, the learned Advocate for the appellant and the learned Advocate for the claimant.
Perused the papers on record.
3) There is no dispute in respect of the extent of land and the purpose for which it is acquired.

Since the Special Land Acquisition Officer (SLAO) granted the rate of Rs.18,000/- per hectare, the respondent/claimant preferred the reference application under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 in short LAC for enhanced compensation.
The appellant filed written statement to the reference.
Necessary evidence was led by the respondent/claimant before the Reference Court.
Considering the judgment and Award dated 28/02/2008 in the Reference No.5 of 1998, the learned Reference Court awarded the compensation @ 50,000/- per hectare to the respondent/claimant.
Kavita.

3/4 14 fa 14-15  4) It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the appellant that the learned Reference Court did not appropriately appreciated the evidence on record and allowed the reference application partly.
He submitted that the impugned judgment and Award was based on the previous judgment passed by the Reference Court arising out of the same award.
He submitted that the appeal be allowed.

5) It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the respondent/claimant that the learned Reference Court has rightly considered it's previous judgment, which was not assailed by the acquiring body and therefore, there is no question of interfering in the impugned judgment and award and the appeal be dismissed.
6) There is no dispute in respect of the purpose for which the respondent's land was acquired by the appellant.
There is also no dispute in respect of the extent of the land of the respondent/claimant acquired for the said purpose.
The impugned judgment show that the learned Reference Court considered the rate of Rs.50,000/- per hectare from Kavita.
4/4 14 fa 14-15 the judgment dated 28/02/2008 in Land Acquisition Reference Case No.5 of 1998.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Reference Case No.5 of 1998
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The papers show that the said judgment below Exh. 53 i.e. in LAC No.5 of 1998 was in respect of the land acquired for the same project.
There is no dispute that the said reference application and the present reference application bearing LAC No.17 of 2012, arose out of the same award dated 21/07/1995 for the same purpose.
There is nothing to show that the judgment and award in the said LAC No.5 of 1998 was set aside by the higher forum.
The enhanced compensation awarded by the learned Reference Court is within four times of the amount of compensation determined by the SLAO.
In the light of above factual undisputed aspects, I find no merit in the said appeal, hence the following order is passed:-
